inclusion.I3: Functional MRI (fMRI) or positron emission tomography (PET) studies
inclusion.I4: Studies examining executive function or cognitive control tasks

inclusion.I5: Functional MRI (fMRI) or positron emission tomography (PET) study assessing executive function or cognitive control using task-based paradigms
inclusion.I6: At least one analysis involving a within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition
inclusion.I7: Whole-brain evidence- At least one analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map
inclusion.I8: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.
inclusion.I9: Tasks must fall within established executive function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation)
inclusion.I10: Relevant information was reported regarding participant age, confirmation of healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI or PET), and task paradigm

exclusion.E3: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no whole-brain results.
exclusion.E4: Studies that report only connectivity analyses (e.g., functional connectivity, PPI, DCM) or resting-state analyses without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only between-group contrasts (e.g., patient vs control) without an accompanying within-group task activation contrast in healthy participants.
exclusion.E6: Studies using rest or fixation as the only baseline condition without an active control task.
exclusion.E7: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human neuroimaging data.
exclusion.E8: Studies including participants outside the age range of 18–60 years or not restricted to healthy individuals.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I1: Whole-brain evidence- The analysis must be from a group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast). Between-group contrasts are acceptable only if they include or clearly reflect a within-group task activation effect in healthy participants.
inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: Contrast or analysis must be relevant to executive function or cognitive control task performance.

exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents)
exclusion.GLOBAL_E3: Analyses not involving executive function or cognitive control processes

inclusion.POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring executive function or cognitive control (example tasks: Working memory tasks, Go/No-Go, Stroop, Task switching, Planning tasks)
inclusion.POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure task-related activation compared to an active control condition (example contrast: Task>control condition)

inclusion.WORKING_MEMORY_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring WORKING MEMORY (example tasks: n-back, delayed match-to-sample)
inclusion.WORKING_MEMORY_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure working memory-related activation compared to a control condition (example contrast: 2-back>0-back)

inclusion.INHIBITION_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring INHIBITORY CONTROL (example tasks: Go/No-Go, Stop-signal, Stroop)
inclusion.INHIBITION_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure inhibition-related activation compared to a control condition (example contrast: No-Go>Go, Incongruent>Congruent)

inclusion.COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring COGNITIVE FLEXIBILITY (example tasks: Task switching, Wisconsin Card Sorting Test)
inclusion.COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure flexibility-related activation compared to a control condition (example contrast: Switch>Repeat)

inclusion.PLANNING_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring PLANNING (example tasks: Tower of London, Tower of Hanoi)
inclusion.PLANNING_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure planning-related activation compared to a control condition

inclusion.VIGILANCE_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring VIGILANCE or sustained attention (example tasks: Continuous Performance Task)
inclusion.VIGILANCE_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure vigilance-related activation compared to a control condition

inclusion.INITIATION_I1: Analyses must be on a task measuring INITIATION (example tasks: verbal fluency, action generation tasks)
inclusion.INITIATION_I2: The analysis/contrast must measure initiation-related activation compared to a control condition
